transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, yeah, thank you. I came in because I've been having a really hard time recently. I was working on this memorial piece for my aunt—she passed away a little while ago, and she was actually the one who convinced me to get my bachelor's in fine arts in the first place. We used to sit on her porch and paint watercolors when I was little. She had this massive wrap-around porch with all these ferns she could never keep alive, which is ironic because she painted them so beautifully... 

But anyway, I was working on her memorial piece, and I just kept getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I was going to dishonor her somehow. Like, it felt like if I made one wrong photo placement or picked the wrong color choice, it would literally mean I didn't love her enough. And I mean, I'm an artist, I get creative doubts all the time, but I couldn't just brush these off like normal. It was just... I don't know, I remember I ran out of my good archival glue right in the middle of it and had to drive all the way across town to the craft store in terrible traffic, and my mind was just racing the whole time about ruining her memory. So, yeah, that's why I decided to make an appointment.
Have you been having these kinds of intrusive, unwanted thoughts in situations other than working on your aunt’s memorial piece?

Um... no, not really. I mean, not that I can think of. It really just started with the memorial piece. I haven't really noticed it with anything else. Although, I did have a hard time deciding what to make for dinner last night, but that's just because I'm terrible at cooking. My partner usually cooks, actually. He makes this amazing vegetarian lasagna. He uses, like, three different kinds of cheese, and he roasts the vegetables first so they get all caramelized. It takes him hours, but it's so worth it. We actually had it for our anniversary last month. We went to this little Italian place for our first date, so it's kind of a tradition now. But yeah, to answer your question, no, I haven't really had those thoughts outside of the memorial project.
Have you noticed any difficulty making decisions or feeling anxious about making mistakes in other areas of your life, even outside of your art?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't think I'm any more anxious about mistakes than anyone else usually. Like, I said, I'm bad at cooking, so I guess I get a little stressed if I have to follow a new recipe. But that's just normal, right? Actually, speaking of recipes, I was trying to bake bread the other day. Sourdough, you know? Everyone got into it a few years ago, but I just started. It's so finicky! You have to feed the starter, and it smells kind of like beer, which reminds me of my dad. He used to brew his own beer in the garage when I was a teenager. It made the whole house smell like yeast and hops. He had all these glass carboys lined up... he even made his own labels for the bottles. He was a graphic designer, so they looked really professional. But anyway, yeah, I don't think I have any major issues with decisions or mistakes outside of that memorial piece. Just the normal stuff.
When you're working on art projects other than the memorial piece, do you ever feel intense anxiety or worry that a small mistake might ruin the whole thing?

Um, no, not really. I mean, like I said earlier, I get normal creative doubts, but nothing intense. Usually, if I mess up a painting, I just paint over it or turn it into something else. That's the beauty of acrylics, they dry so fast. I actually prefer watercolors, though, like the ones I used to do with my aunt. But watercolors are so unforgiving. If you make a mistake with those, you're kind of stuck with it. I tried to teach my niece how to use them last weekend when she came over. She's six, and she just wanted to mix all the colors together until they turned brown. She ended up painting her hands more than the paper. We had to use so much soap to get it off, and it was that nice lavender soap I bought at the farmer's market. There's this woman there who makes all her own soaps and lotions, and she brings her golden retriever to her booth. He's so sweet, he just sleeps under the table the whole time. But yeah, with my regular art, I don't really get that intense worry. Just with the memorial piece.
Do these worries about the memorial piece cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life, like making it hard to focus on anything else or affecting your sleep or relationships?

Um... well, it definitely causes some distress, yeah. I mean, I’m still getting most of my regular work done, but... I just lose so much extra time in the studio now. Like, I’ll be in there for hours just staring at it, trying to get it right. It actually already cost me a grant deadline I was supposed to apply for. The application was so long, anyway. They wanted, like, a ten-page artist statement and a detailed budget. I hate doing budgets. Numbers just kind of blur together for me. My accountant always yells at me because I keep all my receipts in this giant shoebox. It’s an old Nike box from when I tried to take up running a few years ago. I bought all the gear, the shoes, the moisture-wicking shirts... and I think I ran for maybe two weeks before I gave up. It’s just so boring, you know? Just putting one foot in front of the other. I'd rather be doing something creative. But anyway, yeah, missing that grant really sucked. And I also had to back out of a gallery talk I had actually really wanted to do, just because I felt so behind and stressed about the piece. So, I guess it is affecting things a bit.
Outside of working on the memorial piece, have you experienced any other situations where you felt intense distress or anxiety that interfered with your daily activities or relationships?

Um... no, not really. Like I said, it's pretty much just the memorial piece that's got me all tied up in knots. I mean, I get stressed sometimes, like anyone else, but nothing that messes up my whole day. Actually, speaking of my day, I've been trying to get better at organizing my schedule. I bought this really nice planner from a stationery shop downtown. It's got this beautiful leather cover, kind of a deep burgundy color. The shop owner told me it was handmade in Italy. She's so nice, she always remembers my name when I go in. She has this huge collection of vintage fountain pens, too. I bought one from her once, thinking I'd get into calligraphy, but it's so messy. The ink gets everywhere, especially under my fingernails, and it takes days to wash out. I guess I'm just more of a paintbrush kind of person. But yeah, to answer your question, I don't really have that kind of intense anxiety about anything else. Just the sculpture.
Outside of your art and cooking, have you noticed any significant anxiety or difficulty when making everyday decisions, even small ones?

Um, no, not really. I mean, deciding what to wear or what to watch on TV is pretty easy for me. I usually just throw on whatever's comfortable anyway, like these overalls I got from a thrift store last week. They're so soft, and they have all these extra pockets which are great for holding my brushes. I found them in this tiny little shop on the east side of town. The owner there is this older guy who plays jazz music all day on a record player. It's such a cool vibe. He actually had a whole stack of old Miles Davis records by the register. I almost bought one, but then I remembered my record player has been broken for months. The needle snapped when I was trying to dust it, and I just haven't gotten around to ordering a new one. I keep meaning to look it up online, but then I get distracted by something else. But yeah, no big anxiety about small decisions. Just normal stuff.
Have you ever felt anxious or upset about making small, everyday mistakes, even things like sending an email with a typo or wearing something mismatched?

Um, no, not really. If I make a typo in an email, I usually just send a quick 'oops' and move on. It happens to everyone, right? Actually, speaking of emails, I've been getting an insane amount of spam lately. It's just ridiculous. The other day I got one claiming I won a free cruise to the Bahamas. I obviously knew it was a scam, but it really got me thinking about the beach. I haven't been to the ocean in... wow, years. 

I went to Cape Cod when I was a kid with my parents, and we stayed in this adorable little rented cottage that had these bright blue shutters. My mom used to walk down the beach every morning to collect seashells and put them in glass jars on the windowsill. She had this one specific jar that was just full of sea glass—all these beautiful, frosted greens and pale blues. I actually tried to incorporate some sea glass into a mixed-media piece I did back in college, but the epoxy I used totally yellowed over time and ruined the whole aesthetic. I was so mad, I had to scrap the entire project. 

But anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, right, typos and everyday mistakes. Yeah, no, little things like that don't bother me at all.
Have you ever felt anxious or upset about things not being done perfectly, even in small or seemingly unimportant ways, like a door not being fully closed or a line in a drawing not being straight?

Um, no, not really. I mean, if a door isn't shut all the way, I might just close it if there's a draft, but it doesn't upset me. And a crooked line in a drawing? Honestly, sometimes that's the best part. I love happy accidents in art. It reminds me of this time I was taking a pottery class—just for fun, you know, to get my hands dirty. I was trying to throw this perfectly symmetrical vase on the wheel, but my elbow slipped and I totally gouged the side of the clay. I thought it was ruined, but the instructor came over and showed me how to carve into the mistake and make it look intentional. It ended up being my favorite piece from the whole class. I painted it this incredible cobalt blue, but the glaze fired a little weird in the kiln, so it came out looking almost metallic. I actually gave it to my sister for her birthday last year. She has it sitting on her mantelpiece right next to this awful, creepy antique clock her husband bought at a flea market. It chimes every hour and it sounds like something out of a horror movie. I told her she should just take the batteries out, but she says it gives the room character. I don't know how she sleeps through it, honestly. But yeah, no, things don't have to be perfect for me. I'm pretty relaxed about that kind of stuff.
Have you noticed any anxiety, distress, or intrusive thoughts that come up in response to things other than the memorial piece—even if they don't seem related to art or decisions?

Um, no, not really. I mean, besides the memorial piece, I don't really have any intrusive thoughts or, like, weird distress about other stuff. My mind is usually pretty calm, unless I'm trying to figure out what to make for dinner. Speaking of dinner, I went to this new Thai place downtown last night with my friend Sarah. Oh my gosh, the pad thai was incredible, but the portions were so huge! I brought half of it home and put it in the fridge, but my roommate's cat somehow managed to open the container. I swear, that cat is a genius or something. He's this massive orange tabby named Barnaby, and he knows how to open cabinets and doors. The other day, I caught him trying to turn the knob on the bathroom door while I was in the shower. It's hilarious, but also kind of terrifying. Sarah thinks I should get a lock for the fridge, but I feel like that's a bit extreme, right? Anyway, what was the question? Oh, right, anxiety about other things. Yeah, no, I don't think so. Just normal everyday stuff, you know?
Have you noticed any anxiety, distress, or intrusive thoughts when you're reminded of your aunt, even outside of working on the memorial piece?

Not really, no. When I think about her, it's mostly just... normal sad, you know? Like I just miss her. I have this one picture of her on my fridge, actually, and she's standing in her backyard by these massive hydrangea bushes she grew. She was so proud of them. 

I actually tried to grow hydrangeas on my apartment balcony last summer because of that picture, but it was a complete disaster. I think they need way more space, or maybe different soil? I ended up buying this really expensive organic potting mix from the nursery downtown, and I lugged the whole giant bag up three flights of stairs by myself. My arms were sore for like two days. I ended up just using it to repot my snake plant, which is literally the only thing I can keep alive. Honestly, I think my apartment just doesn't get enough natural light because of this huge oak tree right outside my living room window. The squirrels in that tree are so loud in the morning, they literally wake me up before my alarm goes off. They throw acorns at the glass, I swear they do it on purpose... 

But wait, sorry. You were asking about my aunt? Yeah, no, just regular missing her when she comes to mind. No weird anxiety or anything like that.

When you have those intrusive thoughts about dishonoring your aunt while working on the memorial piece, do you feel driven to do something over and over again—like checking, redoing parts, or following certain rules—to reduce the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Um, yeah, I guess I do do that. When I get that feeling, like I'm messing up her memorial, I just... I can't leave it alone. I'll end up rereading the label text I wrote for the piece, like, over and over again. And then I'll start nudging the objects on the display table, just moving them a fraction of an inch this way or that way, and checking the layout photos I took on my phone repeatedly until it finally feels, I don't know, "settled." Even though part of me knows it's already fine, and I'm just completely wasting my studio time. 

Which is so frustrating because studio time is really expensive right now. My landlord just raised the rent on my space by like fifteen percent, which feels totally illegal, but what can you do? I share the space with this other artist, Mark, who does these massive, abstract metal sculptures. He's always using the welding torch, and it smells terrible, like burning ozone or something. Plus, he never takes the trash out. I'm always the one hauling the bins down to the alley. Last week, I found a half-eaten sandwich sitting on his workbench for three days. Three days! I finally had to throw it away because it was attracting fruit flies. I tried making those little traps with apple cider vinegar and dish soap—have you ever tried that? It works surprisingly well, but it smells like a salad dressing exploded in the room. 

Anyway, sorry. But yeah, I do get stuck redoing and checking the memorial stuff until it feels right, even when I know I shouldn't.
Outside of working on the memorial piece, do you ever feel intense distress that something bad might happen if things aren’t done a certain way?

No, not really. Outside of the memorial piece, I don't get that feeling that something bad is gonna happen if I don't do things a specific way. I'm actually pretty laid back about most things. Like, my apartment is kind of a mess right now, to be honest. I was supposed to organize my closet this weekend, but I ended up binge-watching this British baking show instead. It's so relaxing! Have you seen it? The judges are so polite, even when someone's cake completely collapses. 

It made me want to try baking, so I went to the store and bought all this flour and sugar, but then I realized my oven is broken. The landlord was supposed to fix it three weeks ago. He keeps saying he's waiting on a part, but I see him outside watering his lawn every morning, so I don't know how hard he's really trying. His lawn does look amazing, though. It's like a golf course. He uses this special fertilizer that smells awful for the first day, but then it's fine. 

But yeah, anyway, no. I don't really get that intense distress about other things having to be a certain way. Just the memorial piece.
Have you ever felt significant anxiety or distress about intrusive thoughts related to other aspects of your life, even if only briefly or in minor ways?

Um, no, not really. I don't really have those kinds of thoughts about other things. It's really just the memorial piece for my aunt that gets me all... stuck. Like I said, I'm pretty relaxed otherwise. 

Oh, wait, I did get kind of anxious last week, but it wasn't an intrusive thought thing. It was because I lost my favorite scarf on the subway. It was this beautiful hand-knit one my friend Sarah made me for my birthday two years ago. It had these intricate little cable patterns, and the yarn was this gorgeous mustard yellow color. She bought the yarn when she was on a trip to Iceland. Have you ever been to Iceland? She said it was incredible, like being on another planet with all the volcanoes and hot springs. She went to this one lagoon that's supposed to be super good for your skin, and she brought me back this mud mask stuff. I still haven't used it because I'm worried it'll break me out. My skin has been so sensitive lately, probably because of the dry air in my apartment. I bought a humidifier, but it makes this weird gurgling noise all night that drives me crazy. 

But anyway, sorry, I'm rambling again. No, I don't get those distressing intrusive thoughts about other stuff. Just the memorial project.
Have you ever experienced anxiety or distress related to intrusive thoughts in any other area of your life, even if only briefly or mildly?

Um, no, I really haven't. Like I said, it's just the memorial piece. I don't really have those kinds of thoughts about anything else in my life. I mean, my life is pretty normal, mostly. Well, except for the fact that my sister is getting married next month, and she's being a total bridezilla. She wants all the bridesmaids to wear these hideous seafoam green dresses that cost way too much money. And she expects us to pay for them! Plus, the wedding is in this remote barn venue that's supposed to be "rustic chic," but it just means there's no air conditioning and we have to use porta-potties. Can you imagine? In the middle of July? I'm already dreading it. 

I told her she should just have a small ceremony at the courthouse and use the money for a down payment on a house, but she wouldn't listen. She and her fiancé are renting this tiny apartment that doesn't even have a dishwasher. I don't know how they survive. I couldn't live without my dishwasher. Although, honestly, it's been making a weird grinding noise lately, so I should probably get that looked at before it completely breaks down. 

But yeah, anyway... no, no other intrusive thoughts or anything like that. Just the aunt thing.

When you have those intrusive thoughts about dishonoring your aunt while working on the memorial piece, do you feel like you have to do something specific — like arranging objects a certain way, repeating a phrase, or counting — to make the anxiety go away or prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah, I do. It's really frustrating because I know I'm wasting time. When that feeling hits—that I'm somehow disrespecting her memory—I end up rereading the text for the label, like, over and over again. And then I have to nudge the objects on the display table just a tiny bit, and I'll keep checking the layout photos I took. I just keep doing it until it finally feels... settled, I guess. Even though a part of me knows it's perfectly fine and I'm just burning through my studio time. 

Studio time is so expensive right now, too. They just raised the rent on my space by like fifteen percent, which is ridiculous because the heating barely works in the winter. Last January, I had to wear my winter coat and fingerless gloves just to hold a paintbrush. My studio mate, Dave—he does these massive abstract metal sculptures—he actually brought in this little space heater, but it kept tripping the breaker for the whole floor. The building manager was furious. He's this grumpy guy who always smells like stale cigars and peppermint. I don't know why he eats so many peppermints, maybe to cover up the cigar smell? But it doesn't work, it just makes him smell like minty smoke. 

Anyway, yeah, I do those things... rereading the labels and adjusting the pieces until it feels right.

Outside of working on the memorial piece, have you ever experienced intrusive thoughts or urges that cause significant distress or take up a lot of your time, even if they don’t lead to behaviors like checking or repeating things?

Um, no... not that I can think of. It really is just confined to that one memorial project for my aunt. Outside of that, I don't get those distressing thoughts or urges at all. 

I mean, I do get totally absorbed in things sometimes, but that's just part of being an artist, it doesn't upset me. Like, the other day I spent literally four hours trying to mix the exact perfect shade of burnt sienna for a commission I'm doing. It's for this couple who wanted a portrait of their golden retriever, Barnaby. He's such a sweet dog, but he has this very specific reddish tint to his fur that is just impossible to capture. They actually brought him to my studio so I could take reference photos, and he got too excited and ended up knocking over a whole jar of my expensive sable brushes. Water went absolutely everywhere. Thankfully it missed my laptop, but it completely soaked this sketchbook I’ve had since college. I had to spend the rest of the afternoon carefully peeling the pages apart and drying them with a hair dryer. 

My hair dryer is actually on its last legs, now that I think about it. I really need to buy a new one. The cord gets super hot if I leave it on for more than five minutes, which feels like a major fire hazard. I saw one on sale at Target, but it was that really obnoxious hot pink color, and I just prefer my appliances to be neutral, you know? 

But, um, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right. No, no other intrusive thoughts or urges that take up my time or cause me distress. Just the memorial piece.
